Insights

Sen’s Insights as it should be built: a cycle picker, a row of tabs, then each tab’s cards, small ones in pairs and wide ones across. Every card asks its question first and answers it in a line; the chart under it is one accent on grey. Drawn at true size in Minted, with dark and Copper where a second look matters.

1 · This cycleThe tab you land on: five cards, wide ones across and the two small ones side by side. Drawn whole, so the phone is as tall as the tab.

2 · Food, Commitments, Over timeThe other three seeded tabs, settled. The year is a row at the foot of Over time, not a card.

3 · Changing cycleArrows step to the cycle next door; the button between them opens every cycle, each with what was left at its payday. Every tab follows it.

4 · StatesWhat a card does when it’s loading, out of date, empty or broken. The screen around it doesn’t change.

5 · ArrangingA mode, not a screen: the cards stay where they are and gain their controls. Every drag has a tap path.

What I couldn’t make work as written, and what I drew instead

  1. An odd small card. Patterns 4 fills a hole with the next small card, but when a tab has an odd number of small cards there is no next one. The last small card is drawn wide until a partner arrives.
  2. Patterns 7 lists StepPager “for Insights”, and D130 says one card at a time. D152 and D153 replaced both with tabs of cards, so neither is drawn.
  3. D62 chose Insights “over sub-tabs”, and patterns 6 forbids a second tab row. D153 decided the tabs. They’re drawn as chips inside the screen, under the cycle picker, so they read as views of one screen rather than navigation.
  4. “Its change, coloured only where up or down means good or bad.” Patterns 3 keeps the warning colour for over budget and green for money in. So only an over budget is warned, and only saving more than usual is green; every other change is grey, with an arrow and words.
  5. The meal average is “labelled an estimate” (spec 9.3). It has a badge, and its spark is dashed, as every estimate is.
  6. A tab’s Move has no stated form. It opens a short list of places; dragging the chip in arranging does the same.
  7. At 1.5× text two small cards no longer fit side by side, so they stack one to a row. No half row is left, because every card is then full width.
  8. Patterns 7’s app bar has one action. On a past cycle it gains a second, Back to October, because the cycle row has no room once the arrows are in it. On the current cycle the app bar is as before.

Every phone is 390 × 844 unless it says otherwise, scaled to fit the page; a tab taller than the phone is drawn whole. A strip is a piece of a screen at its true width. Inside them every colour, radius and font is the look’s token; the scrim, the shadows and the keyboard stand-in are plain black and grey. Names and amounts are the made-up month the app’s own screenshots use. Source: docs/ui/insights/design-src/.
